Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The study analyzes both native pancreatic tissue and decellularized pancreatic ECM. While the native tissue contains whole cell components, the primary focus and the specific enrichment (ERLIC) target the subproteome of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and its PTMs. Because the material was specifically processed to maximize ECM solubility and then enriched for specific PTM-peptides, it is classified as a subproteome rather than whole cell lysate.

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The primary comparison is between native pancreatic tissue and tissue that has undergone decellularization to isolate the ECM. While decellularization involves chemical agents (deoxycholate/lipase), it is treated here as a state transition (native vs decellularized) to characterize the matrisome. No specific child class in the ontology perfectly matches 'decellularization', so it is mapped to the parent 'cell state or interaction comparison' as it defines the biological group (native vs scaffold).
